inherited_methods.method: Predecessor GC.1 chooses a projective-plane order q only in the interval (K,2K) for N=2^K.
inherited_methods.loss_step: The proof bounds the required point-private primes by a polynomial in K before selecting q, so it never optimizes q against the actual logarithmic size of the odd parts.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Only the logarithm of each selected prime and the logarithm of the number of line codes affect the padding budget; the total number of points affects prime availability but not the size of one integer directly.
inherited_methods.consequence: The recorded blocking number is only q+1>K=log_2 N.

inherited_methods.method: A naive enlargement of q while keeping the predecessor phrase 'choose primes below K^6'.
inherited_methods.loss_step: Once q is larger than a power of K, K^6 no longer contains the q^2 log q point-private primes required by the construction.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The prime cutoff must scale with q, while its logarithm must still fit the K-bit padding budget.
inherited_methods.consequence: The predecessor proof cannot be amplified by changing q alone.

inherited_methods.method: Encode the q+1 incidences at a point by exponents of one or two fixed primes.
inherited_methods.loss_step: Support-minimal path propagation requires enough independent valuation equations at every point, and a fixed-product code with q choices incurs exponent size of order q.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Subset bipartitions encode q choices with only O(log q) private primes and O((log q)^2) total bit cost after prime allocation.
inherited_methods.consequence: Low-dimensional exponent codes permit at most q log q=O(K), much weaker than stretched exponential q.

inherited_methods.method: State the construction only for powers N=2^K.
inherited_methods.loss_step: No monotonicity reduction is recorded for arbitrary N, and the top-band lower endpoint changes when replacing N by the largest lower power of two.
inherited_methods.lost_information: If 2^K<=N<2^(K+1), a support in (2^K/32,2^K] lies in (N/64,N], and every transversal of H_N restricts to one for the embedded subfamily.
inherited_methods.consequence: A sparse-subsequence statement would not satisfy the frozen all-N target.

required_new_information: A quantitative prime-allocation lemma giving at least (q^2+q+1)r distinct odd primes below q^6 for r=ceil(log_2(q+2))+1 and all large q.
An explicit bit-budget inequality showing every point odd part and every two-point private odd part is at most 2^(o(K)) when log_2 q is at most sqrt(K)/100+1.
A padding calculation uniform in this larger q that preserves the band (2^K/32,2^K], equal products, distinctness, and support minimality.
An exact projective-plane hitting calculation and an all-N reduction yielding the stated 2^(sqrt(log_2 N)/200) lower bound.
